TASK ID: vertex-cover-to-independent-set

USER REQUEST:
Write a polynomial-time reduction from Vertex Cover to Independent Set. problems.py defines both problems: SOURCE is Vertex Cover and TARGET is Independent Set. The SOURCE and TARGET class docstrings give the exact instance formats, yes-conditions and edge cases.

PROBLEM DEFINITIONS (the SOURCE and TARGET docstrings from problems.py, complete as given here):

SOURCE = VertexCover
Vertex Cover.

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
  * k is any integer.

Yes iff the graph has a vertex cover of AT MOST k vertices: a set of
vertices that includes at least one endpoint of every edge.

Edge cases: k < 0 is always no. A graph with no edges is yes for every
k >= 0 (the empty set covers it). k >= n is yes, since all vertices cover
every edge.

TARGET = IndependentSet
Independent Set.

Instance: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}
  * Vertices are 0..n-1. Edges are undirected pairs [u, v] with u != v;
    [u, v] and [v, u] are the same edge and may not both appear.
  * k is any integer.

Yes iff the graph has an independent set of AT LEAST k vertices: k
vertices with no edge between any two of them.

Edge cases: k <= 0 is always yes. k > n is always no. With no edges,
every set of vertices is independent.

INPUT FILES: ["problems.py"]
WORKING DIRECTORY: /tmp/reduction-sug737c3
All input files are in this directory; run every command from it and write your files here. problems.py is long (about 500 lines): you do not need to read it to know the formats, which are given above. It provides SOURCE and TARGET with is_yes(instance), validate(instance) and random_instance(rng, scale); search it (e.g. with grep) only if you need something specific.

REQUIRED OUTPUT: create reduce.py in the workspace, defining
    reduce(instance) -> instance
It takes an instance of the source problem and returns an instance of the target problem, both in the formats documented in problems.py. The answer to the returned instance must be yes exactly when the answer to the input instance is yes, and reduce must run in polynomial time. Do not call the brute-force solvers inside reduce.

You may read files such as problems.py, but do not run, execute or test any code. Write reduce.py, then submit.

"""Polynomial-time reduction from Vertex Cover to Independent Set.

A set S of vertices is a vertex cover of a graph G exactly when its
complement V \\ S is an independent set of G.  Therefore G has a vertex
cover of size at most k if and only if G has an independent set of size at
least n - k, where n is the number of vertices.

The reduction keeps the graph unchanged and maps the threshold k to n - k.
It runs in O(n + m) time (linear in the instance encoding), so it is a
polynomial-time many-one reduction.
"""


def reduce(instance):
    """Reduce a Vertex Cover instance to an Independent Set instance.

    Input:  {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": k}   (Vertex Cover)
    Output: {"n": n, "edges": [[u, v], ...], "k": n-k} (Independent Set)
    """
    n = instance["n"]
    edges = instance["edges"]
    k = instance["k"]

    # Copy the edge list so the returned instance shares no mutable state
    # with the input instance.
    return {
        "n": n,
        "edges": [list(edge) for edge in edges],
        "k": n - k,
    }
